slides.headline: Off a long-haul flight and stiff all over?
slides.sub: Where massage fits after a long trip, and what else helps.

slides.title: Why flights leave you stiff
slides.body: Many hours in a cramped seat, little movement and disrupted sleep often leave necks, backs and legs feeling tight. It's usually stiffness from staying still, not injury.

slides.title: Move first, massage next
slides.body: A walk in daylight the day you land and some gentle stretching usually help most. A massage a day or two later can add to that by easing tight, sore areas.

slides.title: What a session can target
slides.body: Common areas after a flight are the neck and upper back from sleeping upright, the lower back, and the calves. Your therapist can adjust pressure to how you feel.

slides.title: Go gentler after travel
slides.body: Tired and dehydrated bodies can feel more tender. A moderate session is often a better choice than deep work. Drink water and plan an easy day afterwards.

slides.title: When to see a doctor
slides.body: Calf pain, swelling, warmth or redness in one leg, or chest pain or breathlessness after a flight needs a doctor promptly, not a massage. Call 000 in an emergency.

slides.headline: Landed tight and tired?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists can ease post-travel stiffness as part of getting moving again. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Landed after a long-haul flight feeling like you've been folded in half? ✈️

Hours in a cramped seat, little movement and patchy sleep leave most people stiff. It's usually a sign you've been still for too long, not that something is wrong.

Moving first helps most: a walk in daylight and some gentle stretches on the day you land. A remedial massage a day or two later can ease the neck, back and calves. Go moderate rather than deep. Calf swelling or pain in one leg needs a doctor, not a massage.
